title: DSA: Linear vs Binary Search
description: Searching is a fundamental operation in computing. Linear search checks every element (O(n)), while Binary Search is significantly faster (O(log n)) but requires the data to be sorted. Binary search works by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half.
example:
// Binary Search Algorithm
def binarySearch(array, x, low, high):
    while low <= high:
        mid = low + (high - low) // 2
        if array[mid] == x: return mid
        elif array[mid] < x: low = mid + 1
        else: high = mid - 1
    return -1

# Optimized search
arr = [2, 3, 4, 10, 40] # Sorted
print(binarySearch(arr, 10, 0, len(arr)-1))
